idiom_name: phantom state parameter + implicit =:= evidence per transition
implementation_notes: Scala's type system supports the pattern directly but asks the programmer to build the evidence: a class carries a phantom state parameter (class Door[S <: State]) and each transition demands an implicit proof that the current state matches (using ev: S =:= Closed), or the state becomes a path-dependent type member. The value-level form uses a sealed state trait plus exhaustive match. Erasure makes the phantom parameter free at run time, but the evidence plumbing appears in every signature, and research implementations had to extend the Scala 3 compiler with capabilities to make the style ergonomic - a sign that the plain-language realization is hand-written rather than idiomatic.
pitfalls: Without the =:= evidence parameter the transition compiles in every state; one forgotten guard silently disables the whole encoding.
Erasure means Door[Open] and Door[Closed] are the same runtime class; asInstanceOf forges states, and a covariant wrapper can widen the state away.
Scala 3 match types and inline can replace =:= evidence with different inference and error behaviour; mixing the two styles in one API makes the protocol hard to read.
